dial.summary: BTC Accumulation holds on Sep 7 (Labor Day): 5 of 8 indicators supportive — Global M2 still expanding, 2s10s confirmed at +41bps (steepening), Fed balance sheet stable at $6.74T, BTC funding rates near zero at 0.007%, and stablecoin dominance in a sustained 30-day downtrend from 13–14% to 11.05%; BTC.D firm at 57.81% (rejected 60% resistance, now consolidating mid-50s), BTC near $79,917 with ETF inflows $3.8B over three weeks; US markets closed today for Labor Day — next data catalyst cluster: ECB Sep 10, CPI Sep 11, FOMC Sep 16, which remain the decisive tests for the macro regime.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) estimated at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; 6–8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); MacroMicro confirmed June global M2 at $102.7T; US M2 June 2026 confirmed at $23.16T (+5.6% YoY, record high, 28th consecutive monthly increase per GlobalMktObserv / FRED); US M2 July 2026 at $23.22T (prior source); global broad money growing at ~12% YoY as of early 2026 (GoldSilverHQ, Feb 2026); 4-week uptrend confirmed (June $102.7T → July estimate $103.4T = +$0.7T, above flat threshold); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; August global 4-bank aggregate not yet published (expected mid-October); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); ECB Sep 10 (possible hike) and FOMC Sep 16 are the next catalysts for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; slightly below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); reading of 54.6% corresponds to approximately 2.4% annualized real GDP growth; next release October 1 (September ISM Manufacturing PMI).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY closed at 99.30 on September 4, 2026 (Friday, NFP day; US markets closed Sep 5–7 — weekend + Labor Day); DXY rebounded on the day after August NFP beat (+162K vs +56K consensus) reversed the prior week's ADP-driven decline (DXY had dipped to 99.37 on Sep 3 after the ADP miss); 4-week trend down: from approximately 101.0–101.4 in early August 2026 to 99.30 on Sep 4 = −1.7% to −2.0% relative decline, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status neutral (ICE DXY 99.30 within the 97.5–100 neutral band); next trading data on Sep 8 (Tuesday); a DXY break above 100 (e.g. hot CPI Sep 11 or FOMC hike Sep 16) would shift status to headwind; a break below 97.5 would shift to supportive.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield): 2.45% as of September 2, 2026 (last confirmed; Sep 4 data pending FRED publication on Sep 8 — markets were open Sep 4 for NFP but FRED typically publishes the following business day); after strong Aug NFP (+162K), nominal 10Y moved to ~4.76–4.78% while BEI held around 2.34%, implying Sep 4 TIPS ~2.42–2.44% — within rounding of 2.45%; 4-week trend flat: ~2.43% (Aug 4 estimate) → 2.45% (Sep 2) = +2bps, within the 5bps flat threshold; status neutral (flat trend means 'rising AND above 2%' headwind condition not fully triggered; 'falling or below 1%' supportive condition not met); next confirmed update: Sep 8 (FRED publishes Sep 4 and Sep 5 data after Labor Day).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 4, 2026 (Friday, last trading day before Labor Day weekend): 2s10s spread confirmed at +0.41% (+41bps) per T10Y2Y FRED data and multiple sources; 10Y yield ~4.78%, 2Y yield ~4.37%; markets closed Sep 5–7 (weekend + Labor Day); 4-week steepening trend: ~+35bps (Aug 4 estimate per prior run) → +41bps (Sep 4) = +6bps steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening confirmed; well outside the −50bps headwind threshold); next market data Sep 8 (Tuesday); a Fed hike Sep 16 (market-implied probability ~52% after NFP beat) would likely flatten the curve as 2Y re-prices faster than 10Y.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T for week ending September 3, 2026 (H.4.1 released September 3 at federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/current/; prior week Aug 26 was $6.73T, Aug 19 was $6.70T per govspending.org/convextrade.com); 4-week trend flat: Aug 5 estimate ~$6.70T → Sep 3 $6.74T = +$40B, within flat threshold; next H.4.1 (week ending Sep 10) releases Sep 10 at 4:30 PM ET alongside ECB decision and PPI; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; routine measured QT continues with no acceleration and no overnight rate spike); FRED API blocked this run — H.4.1 value sourced from secondary web aggregates confirming the Sep 3 release.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately +0.007% per 8h (CoinGlass direct fetch blocked via egress proxy; value carried from prior run consistent with market context); BTC price ~$79,917 (Sep 6; CoinStats/CoinGecko) with BTC.D at 57.81% (Sep 6–7 per multiple aggregators; BTC.D surpassed 60% briefly in 2026 before pulling back, acting as near-term resistance); firm BTC.D and roughly flat BTC price consistent with near-zero funding (no leveraged long pressure, spot-driven accumulation); 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August–September 2026; well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding confirms spot-driven price action); alt-rotation trigger not met (BTC.D 57.81% well above 55% threshold).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $307B (Sep 6–7, 2026; CoinGecko global charts); total crypto market cap $2.77T (Sep 6–7; CoinGecko — declined from $2.79T in prior run); stablecoin dominance 11.05% ($307B / $2.77T); 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 to 11.05% = sustained ~2–3pp decline reflecting capital deployment into risk assets; week-over-week: 10.98% (Sep 6) → 11.05% (Sep 7) = +0.07pp noise driven by TOTAL market contraction (stablecoin market cap unchanged while crypto market cap dipped), within the clear 30-day downtrend; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL also rising — does not apply: TOTAL declined from $2.79T to $2.77T); BTC.D at 57.81% remains firm; USDT and USDC dominate stablecoin supply.

upcoming.title: PPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — pipeline inflation read one day before CPI (Sep 11) and six days before FOMC (Sep 16); July 2026 PPI was unchanged (final demand goods −0.7%, services +0.2%); August NFP beat (+162K vs +56K consensus, Sep 4) reset rate expectations to ~52% market-implied probability of a Sep 16 hike; a hot PPI print would reinforce the hike case and could push DXY above 100 (headwind threshold); a cooling PPI would add to the disinflationary narrative and reduce hike probability heading into CPI Sep 11; released same day as ECB rate decision (2:15 PM CET) and weekly jobless claims.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 6, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 6, 2026 (note: week ended on Saturday Sep 6, reported Thursday Sep 10); prior week ending Aug 29 came in at 206,000; strong August NFP (+162K, Sep 4) confirmed labor market resilience; a spike in claims above 220K would temper the rate-hike narrative heading into CPI Sep 11 and FOMC Sep 16; released alongside PPI August and ECB rate decision — a triple-event day.

upcoming.title: ECB Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: European Central Bank Governing Council rate decision at 2:15 PM CET (8:15 AM ET), press conference at 2:45 PM CET; Reuters poll (Sep 3) showed 65 of ~90 economists expecting a 25bps hike to the deposit rate; an ECB hike alongside a hot US PPI on Sep 10 would reinforce the global tightening narrative and could push DXY above 100 (headwind threshold for risk assets); ECB guidance on the pace of further tightening and updated staff projections on inflation will drive EUR/USD and global fixed income impact; also released same day: H.4.1 Fed balance sheet (week ending Sep 10) at 4:30 PM ET.

upcoming.title: CPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — final major inflation read before FOMC September 16; the data trifecta: NFP Sep 4 (+162K, hawkish), CPI Sep 11, then FOMC Sep 16; markets pricing ~52% probability of a hike after NFP beat; a hot CPI above 3.8% YoY would likely lock in a Sep 16 hike and push DXY above 100 (headwind for risk assets); a soft CPI below 3.3% would pull back hike expectations and support risk assets; July 2026 PCE (released Aug 26) was 3.7% YoY; core CPI ex-food and energy is the primary Fed focus; DXY currently at 99.30 — the Sep 11 and Sep 16 events are the key triggers for a directional break.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Survey preliminary read for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — released same day as CPI August; captures 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations alongside current conditions and expectations indexes; elevated 1-year inflation expectations combined with hot CPI would strengthen the Fed's case for a Sep 16 hike; a drop in confidence alongside cooling CPI would temper hike odds and create a risk-asset supportive setup heading into FOMC; watch 5-year inflation expectations closely as a long-run anchoring signal for the Fed's reaction function.
